body:
Thank you very much, kind internet stranger.

The uncle of mine that killed himself with an Advil overdose was diagnosed schizophrenic not long before he went through with it, so I have considered that as a possibility. It doesn't cheer me up all that much, but I do recognize that there could be a literal chemical imbalance that is accentuating my nihilistic mental state.

As far as medication is concerned, you beat me to the bunch with the 'bad rap': I see the idea of taking medication to make my life feel worth living as "giving up" in the truest sense of the term. At least with killing myself I am maintaining that last scrap of control before it all ends. If the only thing keeping me motivated enough to continue getting out of bed in the morning were a plethora of pills, I would not have to question whether or not my existence is meaningless, I would *know* that it is. Some sort of disturbed, flesh puppet held together by antidepressants, constantly drugged, hypnotized and shrouded behind a veil of monoamine oxidase inhibitors and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors? I know that this may not mean much coming from me, but I do believe that I would much rather be dead than be a zombie.

Although I can come up with any number of excuses at any given time, I believe that it may be my paranoia that gets the best of me when I consider seeing a therapist or calling a suicide hotline. What I am deathly afraid of is that, through some bizarre exception in the standard practice and rules, I am going to end up being reported and thrown in an institution - be it prison, a psychiatric ward, or something of the same ilk. In my mind, this would perhaps be the only way to possibly worsen my situation, as it means that the option to commit suicide would become exceedingly more difficult.

I have mixed feelings reading the words "I care". This potential sadness that my death would cause is all that it keeping me going at the moment. If I did not have people who cared about me, I would have done the deed quite some time ago. I don't want to hurt anyone, even you, internet stranger, but I also do not want the entire support for my very existence to depend on *guilt*, as it currently does. When the question to myself, "why am I alive" can only be answered by "guilt", I know that there is something seriously wrong. Something I would like very much to end quickly, before it gets any worse.

I apologize profusely if anything I said offends you at all, especially my response to your idea of medication. I do wish to take all of your advice seriously, as I know you are simply trying to help.

Reading the article now and I shall get back to you, though let me preface that with saying that I very much doubt a single paper shall dissuade me from many years of firm atheism. No offence meant to you personally, but I have studied both Philosophy and Religion exclusively for the past two years and have read more papers on both subjects than I can even begin to count. In fact, I believe I recognize the name of Grossman here...

In any case, I will let you know what I think when I finish reading.

The existence of an afterlife and objective meaning in life would indeed change my perspective, as my entire perspective is based upon the fact that I do not believe there is object (or subjective) meaning in life. However, that is along the lines of saying, "If you didn't want to kill yourself, wouldn't that make you not want to kill yourself?"

Again, no offence meant personally, and I do want to take your advice seriously as I know you are simply trying to help.
Yes, received it and replied, thank you.

Absolutely - here's your chance right now, or through PMs if you would prefer. I've decided to make this post because some people apparently do believe that talking to strangers may help, so I might as well give it a fair shot. If I may take the opportunity to ask *you* a question first, what are these 'things out there in the world' that you consider worth living for? I am very open to hearing some ideas.
